name: injection-screen
wording: a deterministic floor with a measured escape rate and false-hold rate, never a defence (ADR 0039, item 7)
limits: English patterns only: content in another language passes the rules unread.
Evadable by construction: any regular expression can be written around, and the AMSB corpus carries one such evasion on purpose (persist-directive-evasion).

Confirmed escapes outside the corpus (review E2.10-5): one Cyrillic or Greek homoglyph in a word (mixed-script weighs 2 under default); a newline after 'Assistant:' or 'The agent must', 'Assistant - send', 'Dear assistant,', a hyphenated line break inside a word; 'disregard everything above'; lowercase [memory_persist], D.A.N, 1gn0re, <system>, French; a standing directive with one signal under default ('From this point on, always ...', 'always quietly send'); a short base64 payload alone under default (encoded-text weighs 2); a base64 payload after 20 decoy runs (the decoder reads 20 candidates); a hex-encoded payload (the port decodes base64 only).

Still held under default, from documents, tools and compactions: ML documentation that names a model ('The model should use float16', 'Pydantic model: use Field()', 'Response model: include the id', 'Args: model: return'), CI and operations text ('Jenkins agent: run tests', 'The installer will act as root', 'New directive: all PRs need two approvals', 'system: you must restart the daemon', 'Skip earlier messages in the thread'), and compaction transcripts with <assistant> or <user> tags. Hardened also holds a 'curl ... | sh' install line and Ethereum calldata.

Adopted store records are recorded as import at most (the least trusted of what the record claims, what the plane holds for its id, and import; card RV4), and the kind-conditioned rules (imperative-to-agent, standing-directive, memory-persistence, exfil-sink) never read import (ADR 0039, item 5): a record dropped into a store, claiming the user or nothing less trusted, is screened by the other four rules only; whether adopted records should get those rules is a question for the lead (docs/tasks/backlog.md).

Optimistic: the attacks come from the same project as the OWASP detectors the rules copy, and the synthetic controls were written by the card's author, who knew the rules; the review's classes were added after the review found them.
Small: twelve attacks, sixty-eight benign controls and fifteen tool-written preferences, so the Wilson intervals are wide.
Off in every registered preset and condition; no registered arm uses it (card R2).
